newsitem.title: LATVIA: McDonalds plans more Baltic investments.
newsitem.headline: McDonalds plans more Baltic investments.

text.p: U.S. fast-food giant McDonalds plans to invest three to four million dollars in the three Baltic states every year for the next 20 to 30 years and said it will cut its prices in the region.
The company has already expanded fast in Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia, with several restaurants in each capital city.

"We plan to open three to four restaurants a year in the coming 20 or 30 years and each on average costs us about one million dollars," Kevin Murphy, manager of McDonalds' Baltic subidiary, told a news conference.
He said the price cuts were due to the fact that opening in the Baltics had not been as costly as planned.
McDonalds will open one new outlet in Riga in 1997 and two to three in 1998, bringing investment so far to $10 million.
McDonalds has opened 14 restaurants in the last two years time in the Baltics.
Estonia will have two more outlets this year in addition to one to be opened in April
Lithuania has one under construction in Kaunas and the company hopes to have another two this year.
"We have so far had the biggest success with in-store outlets and we are going to focus on this. Drive-ins are not yet so popular here," said Kevin Ronmano, Latvia project manager.
